scenes.say: Your pull request passed review. The checks are green. But what if a model, dependency, or provider around it changed five minutes ago?
Releases stall when yesterday's approval meets today's reality. Someone still has to connect the dots, find the owner, and decide what happens next.
Drift C I is an automatic project manager for software releases. It watches GitHub pull requests, reviews and C I alongside the official web, keeping every task tied to the exact commit.

Instead of another feed, Drift C I creates an evidence-backed work queue. See what changed, which files it touches, what needs review, and what can wait. Every arrival joins one durable live timeline.

Context dot dev retrieves the official model lifecycle, pricing, S D K release and provider status pages relevant to the repository. Drift C I keeps snapshots, source receipts and genuine before-and-after diffs, so the team can verify every signal.

For vulnerabilities, Drift C I combines O S V and CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities with repository evidence. Affected versions, reachability clues, an ordered checklist and an exportable incident record turn an advisory into response work, while keeping uncertainty visible.

A named reviewer records ready or hold for an exact pull request head, C I snapshot and evidence fingerprint. A later commit, check result or external change expires that decision automatically. Drift C I automates the follow-up while the human keeps the release call.
Drift C I. Your release project manager and vulnerability auditor. Less coordination. Faster vulnerability triage. Evidence that is still true when you ship.
